correctness.rationale: The original mathematical computations held up. I independently used the bipartite disjointness cover on pairs, monotone synchronous closure, generator closure on all triples, and all-source distance layers in each exchange graph. All 211 smaller seeds fail; all 1,140 triples split into twelve orbits, of which just two succeed, with counts and times (120,3) and (120,2). Both edge sets, all-source eccentricities and original table entries agree. The repaired proof isolates the timing and local slide results. It uses the independently confirmed baseline census and its transitivity. Adjacency in the subset model is Hamming distance one; monotone alternating insertion/deletion paths inside the middle levels achieve Hamming distance between any two masks. The listed initialization masks and exact subsequent singleton-neighbor additions were verified at both representatives. With three nonadjacent selected vertices of degree three, the nine replacement candidates at each representative are exhaustive; classification by the two feasible profiles gives exactly two within-type and two cross-type slides. By automorphism transitivity these checks apply to every minimum state. The two-round deadline thus keeps exactly half of the full slide degree in the feasible states. The claimed degree and eccentricity trade-off uses the full optimal-state graphs, not their deadline-restricted subgraphs.
residual_risks: Rounds are counted after the initial closed-neighborhood observation. The repaired finding gives no connectivity or diameter assertion for the deadline-restricted graph. The bundled programs use int.bit_count and hence Python 3.10 or newer (the frozen 3.9 claim was too permissive).

value.rationale: Minimum sensor count alone treats the two orbits identically. A natural next objective is to minimize time to full observation without buying another sensor, and to know how many optimized placements are locally reachable by a single slide while meeting that time constraint. The repair gives the fastest deadline, identifies exactly which orbit meets it, and determines the local degree loss from four to two everywhere in that orbit. This is useful exact data about the interaction of two different objectives, not a repeat of full-graph diameter or a claim about a global restricted radius. The broader frozen census and main full-graph metrics do not qualify as separate new contributions.
residual_risks: Local deadline-preserving branching only, on this specific twenty-vertex graph. No general propagation/mobility trade-off theorem is inferred.
